scope: This build adds comprehensive accessible release documentation and Braille copies. Keyboard instructions below also describe features already available in the comparison build; they are labeled as current references rather than new application changes.

topics.title: Accessible release notes in six formats.
details: Every new build includes these release notes as TXT, HTML, Word DOCX, EPUB, text-only DAISY 3, and BRF. All print and digital text editions use the same reviewed source; the BRF contains a Braille translation of that source.

The outline follows the supplied BrailleSense reference: a release title at heading level 1; New Apps and Features and Fixes and Enhancements at heading level 2; numbered topics; and lettered details beneath each topic. Topic numbering restarts in each major section, and detail lettering restarts for each topic. The TXT edition displays those numbers and letters as ordinary text.

In Word, use heading navigation to move between the title and major sections. In HTML and EPUB, use heading navigation or the linked contents. In DAISY, open the extracted guide.opf in a player supporting text-only DAISY 3. The DAISY edition uses the same two heading levels and nested numbered and lettered lists. It contains text for the player to speak rather than recorded narration.

The notes identify the version, release date, comparison build, testing or official status, and the scope of changes. New release notes must be reviewed and updated for each version: the builder rejects notes belonging to another version. A testing build is not described as an official stable release.

topics.title: Braille copies of the manual and release notes.
details: START HERE - Veteran.brf and Voice Companion Release Notes.brf are now produced during the installer build. These are genuine six-dot ASCII BRF files translated with Liblouis using contracted Unified English Braille, also called UEB grade 2. They are not print text renamed with a .brf extension.

The Braille copies use 40 cells per line, 25 lines per page, and form-feed page separators. Open them on a Braille device or in a BRF reader that supports this layout. Print typographic quotation marks and dashes are normalized before translation. Words, shortcuts, numbers, and letters remain part of the source content.

The translator is a build tool. People installing Voice Companion do not need to install Liblouis, and it does not become another synthesizer choice. A build fails if translation or BRF validation fails, rather than distributing a missing or placeholder Braille copy.

These files are mechanically translated. They have not undergone a human Braille proofreading or embosser-specific production review. For literal spelling of an unfamiliar command, filename, email address, or URL, consult the matching TXT edition when needed.

topics.title: Where to find the documentation.
details: Installation and updates copy the current manual and release notes into Documents, Voice Companion, User Guides. Windows supplies the Documents location, including a redirected Documents folder. A successful new installation replaces the shipped documentation there with the current build copies.

Use the Voice Companion User Guides shortcut on the desktop or Start menu, or say open user guides from the app. You can also press Alt+T, type open user guides, and press Enter. Personal files placed in that folder are preserved.

The GitHub release includes the manual and release-note files as separate downloads as well as the installer. You can read or share documentation without installing the app. The release page itself contains the detailed print release notes.

The release publisher requires all twelve documentation files before uploading. It verifies the uploaded files before making a release visible to the automatic updater. Missing notes, missing formats, or a mismatched version prevent publication.

topics.title: Email keyboard reference: open, compose, and send.
details: The following shortcuts describe the current email controls introduced in 0.2.96-test. They are documented here for clarity; 0.2.97-test does not add a new set of mail actions. First open Email from the main menu and select or connect an account.
Ctrl+Y opens the folder chooser. Use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to choose a folder, then Enter to open it. F5 reloads the message list for the current folder. Ctrl+N starts a new email.

With a message current, Ctrl+R starts a reply; Ctrl+Shift+R starts a reply to all; and Ctrl+F starts a forward. These shortcuts are available while reading a received message as well as from its message list.

To move to a draft field using the keyboard, press Alt+T, type go to to, go to cc, go to bcc, go to subject, or go to body, then press Enter. These use the same commands available by voice. In an address field, type the address and press Enter to accept it. Body editing uses ordinary Windows text editing keys.

Ctrl+Enter in a draft requests Send. It does not bypass the normal send confirmation. Answer the confirmation before sending. Escape cancels a draft without saving it; Escape while reading a received message returns to its message list.

Mail keyboard actions continue to work while the microphone sleeps and in Dictation Only mode. Direct text editing applies to documents and draft bodies. Received email text can be navigated and selected, but it is read-only.

topics.title: Email keyboard reference: select, delete, and move messages.
details: In the message list, Space marks or unmarks the current message. This action applies when the typed command field is empty. Shift+Up Arrow and Shift+Down Arrow extend the message selection while moving through the list.

Ctrl+A in the message list selects all messages on the currently loaded page. It does not select every message in the account. Ctrl+A inside received-message text or an editable text body selects text instead of messages.

Delete in the message list requests deletion of the current message or selected messages. A Yes or No question must be answered. Messages are moved to the provider Trash or Deleted Items folder; this shortcut is not a permanent-delete command.

Ctrl+Shift+V opens the destination folder chooser to move the current or selected messages. Choose a folder with the arrows and Enter, then answer the confirmation. This is a mail action, separate from the ordinary Ctrl+V text paste shortcut.

For a Yes or No question, use the arrows or Tab and Shift+Tab to choose an answer, then Enter or Space to accept it. Escape cancels the question. You can also say yes or no, or type the answer into the command field and press Enter. Typing no must not accept a preselected Yes.

topics.title: Email keyboard reference: create, rename, and delete folders.
details: Ctrl+Shift+E opens the Create Folder prompt. Type the name and press Enter, or say the name using the folder command. Review and answer the confirmation before the provider is changed.

F2 in Email opens the Rename Folder chooser. Select the folder with the arrows and Enter, type its new name, and press Enter. Review the Yes or No confirmation. F2 in a document names the document instead; its action depends on the current area.
Ctrl+Shift+D opens the Delete Folder chooser. Choose the folder and answer the confirmation. Delete while a folder chooser is open requests deletion of the highlighted folder.

Standard provider folders are protected. Folder deletion is restricted to empty user-created folders with no child folders. If the app refuses to delete a populated or protected folder, move its messages or use the provider interface as appropriate; refusal is intentional protection.

The matching voice commands include create folder followed by its name, rename folder, rename to followed by the new name, and delete folder. Use next or previous and okay, confirm, confirm that, or that one for a chooser. Alt+T lets you type the same commands and press Enter.

topics.title: Release documentation generation and publication.
details: Previously, the published release description was a short generic installer message. New releases now use reviewed, version-specific notes that describe changed behavior, how to use relevant commands and shortcuts, where files are installed, and material limitations.

The document builder creates all six release-note formats together and creates a BRF manual alongside the existing five manual editions. Shared source text prevents the formats from describing different features or shortcut mappings.

The numbered and lettered labels in the supplied reference are generated list formatting, not literal characters stored in the paragraph text. The new release-note exporter reproduces the list hierarchy instead of dropping those labels during text extraction.

Publication stops if the notes version differs from the application version. Future maintainers must update release-notes.json for each build, describe actual changes since the named baseline, and retain the distinction between testing and official releases. Changing only the version number is not sufficient editorial review.

Installer copying, application guide discovery, separate GitHub assets, and release verification all include the additional document files. An app update can therefore refresh the accessible release notes and Braille manual in the same location as the other guide formats.

topics.title: Verify guide refresh after automatic updates.
details: Guide discovery previously checked that filenames existed, without verifying the documentation version or content. It could prefer a copy beside the executable over the bundled copy. Those checks did not establish that the copies in Documents matched the running build.

The builder now creates a documentation manifest containing the version and SHA-256 checksum of every manual and release-note file. The app checks that manifest and chooses files matching its version and checksums. A stale alternative copy cannot silently overwrite the current guide with old content.

Setup now runs a hidden documentation refresh after copying application files, including during a silent automatic update. This refresh does not open the microphone or start another interactive app window. Normal app startup and the Open User Guides command also copy and verify the current documentation.

The Windows build checks the installed documentation refresh before publishing. In Documents, Voice Companion, User Guides, documentation-version.json records the successfully verified version and file checksums. The print manual also shows its guide build near the beginning so you can identify an old copy.

If a file is locked open or Documents is unavailable, the app cannot guarantee replacement until the problem is resolved. Close any guide reader, then reopen User Guides or restart the app to retry. A failed refresh writes user-guide-update-error.txt under Local AppData, VoiceCompanion; stale copies are not reported as successfully updated. A reader already displaying a guide may need to close and reopen it to load the replaced file.

topics.title: Current document saving and exit behavior: keyboard reference.
details: These controls were introduced in 0.2.96-test and are restated to explain the current behavior. F2 while writing a document opens its naming field. Type the name and press Enter, or say the name and confirm. The filename changes and you return to editing; the name is not inserted into the document body.

Escape or the voice command main menu while editing asks whether you want to save. Yes opens the naming step before leaving. No discards changes made since the document was opened or last explicitly saved. Escape at the question cancels the exit and keeps you in the document.

An existing document retains the previously saved file when changes are discarded. A new unsaved document is removed rather than left as an unwanted untitled file. The discarded session is cleared so Resume does not bring those changes back.

Exit Voice Companion is the last main-menu item. The commands close companion, exit companion, and return to windows request exit. Alt+F4 or closing the app window also requests exit. If a document is open, the save question comes first.

Enter and Escape are contextual. Enter in a naming field accepts its text; Enter in a chooser opens the highlighted option; Escape in a document starts the save question; and Escape in a mail draft cancels that draft. Do not assume Escape has the same save behavior in every area.

topics.title: Current text navigation and speech settings: keyboard reference.
details: In a document, draft body, or received message, Left and Right Arrow move by character; Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right move by word; Up and Down Arrow move by display line; and Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down move by paragraph. Home and End move within the line; Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End move to the beginning or end of the text. Shift with a movement key extends text selection.

Ctrl+Comma opens the self-voicing settings dialog. Focus starts in the category list. Up and Down Arrow change category without requiring Enter. Tab and Shift+Tab move through that category controls. Space toggles checkboxes, and the arrows change radio or combo choices. Enter accepts OK; Cancel or Escape leaves without applying pending dialog changes.

Verbosity contains punctuation, typing echo, and delayed phonetic character feedback. Typing echo can announce words, characters, characters and words, or none. Phonetic feedback can be enabled or disabled and its delay adjusted; the default delay is half a second.

High verbosity provides fuller navigation guidance. Medium uses shorter hints. Low omits optional navigation hints. These presets do not remove document or email content, important questions, or errors, and do not replace your independently chosen typing echo, punctuation, or phonetic settings.

Press Alt+T anywhere a typed command field is available to focus it, type an app command, and press Enter. This supplies a keyboard path for actions that do not have a dedicated shortcut. Menu and list navigation uses arrows and Enter, with spoken item names followed by their positions.

topics.title: Testing status, update instructions, and limits.
details: 0.2.97-test remains a testing build. This release changes documentation generation, packaging, and publication; it does not intentionally change speech recognition, email provider authentication, or the application editing commands.

Install VoiceCompanion-Setup.exe or accept the offered automatic update. Download progress is announced in five-percent increments. You can request update status or status during the update. Keep the machine connected and allow the update process to finish before checking the new version.

Email still depends on the configured Gmail or Microsoft application permissions and provider policies. This documentation release does not remove Gmail testing-user restrictions or Microsoft organization approval requirements. People must use their own authorized email accounts.

The notes describe implemented behavior and automated validation, not a guarantee for every microphone, headset, account, DAISY player, Braille display, or embosser. Report the app version, the command or shortcut used, the current area, the expected result, and what actually happened when testing.

Before publication, the Windows builder must pass its application tests, package the installer, install it for its runtime check, and verify release assets. These notes are prepared before those checks run; the final release log provides the actual test outcome.
